purpose: Replace benchmark-visible flat Cube futon placeholders with ordinary circa-2000 household bedding draped over the final rendered balcony handrail. This contract specifies construction and installation logic only; it does not assert a specific manufacturer or award rendered-quality credit.

components: lofted batting/fill represented by closed 22 mm render thickness under gravity/compression
stitched quilting and edge-binding microstructure represented by textile normal response rather than painted lighting
manufacture.constructionLogic: A flexible filled textile is modeled as a continuous closed ribbon with two outer faces plus side and end hems. It bends around the rail under gravity instead of remaining a planar rigid slab.
manufacture.geometryVsMaterial: Centimetre-scale loft, rail wrap, front/back drops, gravity sag, silhouette and closed hems are geometry. Thread weave, fine quilting/stitch impression, fibre breakup, UV fading and tiny abrasion are material/normal response. Highlights and folds may not be painted into albedo.

dimensionsThickness.note: Nominal front drops preserve the original 0.770 m rail-center datum. At build time the front drop increases by finalRailCenterAboveFloor - 0.770 m, so raising the reconstructed guardrail to a 1.10 m top does not leave the textile floating hundreds of millimetres above the slab. The two variants retain different balanced drops/sag and do not read as cloned rigid panels.

materials.microstructure: 512 px deterministic asymmetric warp/weft plus fibre-breakup normal, physically tiled at 0.14 m; mipmapped, trilinear and anisotropic
materials.wetness: 0.0 in the benchmark dry midsummer state; no uniform wet sheen
materials.uvAging: moderate exposure fading on outward-facing bedding; represented by restrained base-color family, not directional painted light
materials.angularFresnel: dielectric cloth response only; no metallic edge flash and no baked highlight

materials.finish: dry slightly lighter aged woven bedding textile
materials.microstructure: same manufacture-scale weave family as A but a different visible drape/sag installation; no macro illumination is encoded
materials.wetness: 0.0 in the benchmark dry midsummer state
materials.uvAging: slightly lighter dye state representing household/UV variation without damage narrative
materials.angularFresnel: rough dielectric cloth; grazing response must come from Standard PBR and geometry

mounting.method: gravity-balanced airing placement over the final rendered balcony top rail
mounting.loadPath: front textile drop -> compressed crest/rail wrap -> back textile drop; no invisible rigid bracket is invented
mounting.legacyHandling: Keep each legacy Futon_* GameObject/collider as an occupancy/gameplay anchor but disable its Cube Renderer. Generated drape geometry is render-only and collider-free.
mounting.railReference: QualityBlockBalconyGuardrailInstallationQA.ResolveTopRailBounds(<floor>,<bay>) is the installation datum when the reconstructed guardrail exists; otherwise it falls back to the active legacy RailTop_* renderer for standalone source work.
mounting.heightCompensation: resolvedFrontDropM = nominalFrontDropM + max(0, finalRailCenterAboveFloorM - 0.770). This preserves the intended lower-edge/slab relationship when the physically reconstructed guardrail raises the crest above the old undersized fallback rail.

interfacesGapsSeals.railContact: The inner face of the 22 mm textile loft uses a 51 mm centerline envelope offset. That gives a 40 mm inner envelope, matching the reconstructed 70 x 80 mm top rail depth exactly and remaining within the 12 mm source tolerance of the old 90 x 90 mm fallback datum. Native oblique/grazing pixels must still prove absence of visible air gap or hard interpenetration.
interfacesGapsSeals.floorClearance: The hanging lower edge must remain 0.030-0.090 m above the rendered balcony slab top after resolved rail-height compensation. A lower edge entering the slab is a construction failure, not a weathering effect.
interfacesGapsSeals.sideEnds: Both lateral hems and both hanging ends are closed geometry so 22 mm loft remains visible at oblique angles rather than exposing a zero-thickness sheet.
interfacesGapsSeals.seals: Not applicable; this is an exposed flexible textile assembly.

orientationExposure.orientation: Outward/front drop faces the benchmark camera and exterior summer sun; back drop is more sheltered by the rail/balcony depth.
orientationExposure.sun: Coherent midsummer Japanese directional sun must create cloth form shading from the drape itself; no local painted highlight or contradictory shadow direction is permitted.
orientationExposure.rain: Benchmark state is dry. Historical rain exposure may contribute mild dye/fibre aging but does not justify current wet gloss.
orientationExposure.contact: Rail crest receives local compression/contact occlusion; the lower hem receives no invented ground grime because it clears the slab.

forbiddenAppearance: random structural tears used as detail
aging.causality: Aging must follow textile exposure/use and stay subordinate to construction form.

lod1.role: retain rail wrap and lower silhouette

lod3.role: retain occupancy silhouette; never revert to a Cube/plane

lodPolicy.hardRule: Vertex count must decrease at every LOD and renderer bounds must remain within 18 mm size / 10 mm center of LOD0. Visible pop remains a temporal rendered critical check.

qaRules.renderVerification: PENDING until native 3840x2160 hero/oblique/grazing evidence plus 100% crops exist

renderEvidencePlan.hero: Confirm the old rigid rectangular Cube silhouette is absent and the front drop has gravity sag/cloth shading rather than painted folds.
renderEvidencePlan.oblique: At 100% crop verify 22 mm closed loft, crest wrapping around the reconstructed 70 x 80 mm top rail, side/end hems, slab clearance and no floating/interpenetrating hero geometry.
renderEvidencePlan.grazing: Verify rough dielectric Fresnel, textile normal response without plastic/metallic flash, and no baked highlight.
renderEvidencePlan.temporal: Verify all four LOD transitions retain the same hanging silhouette without visible pop, shimmer or normal-map aliasing.

expectedVisualScoreImpact.geometryConstruction: Potentially removes a critical primitive-placeholder/interpenetration risk and keeps textile installation physically attached after the guardrail is corrected to a realistic height.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.materialPbr: Potentially replaces flat generic material response with rough dielectric textile microstructure.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.periodAuthenticity: Retains ordinary household balcony-airing occupancy without introducing a branded/anachronistic product claim.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.temporalLod: Dedicated four-level cross-faded drape LODs reduce the risk of occupancy silhouette popping.

visualCreditPolicy.reason: Source geometry/material/QA readiness is not rendered evidence. The 100-point Visual Fidelity Gate remains UNSCORED until actual Unity captures are reviewed.
